title: PreToolUse write-guard fails OPEN — agent disables its own guard with 'git config core.bare true'
detail: REPRODUCED end-to-end during review. The repo-target transport exits 0 (=ALLOW for PreToolUse) whenever git rev-parse --show-toplevel fails. The guarded agent can force that from inside the repo: 'git config core.bare true' makes rev-parse exit 128 (verified), $r empty, fail-open arm fires, every subsequent PreToolUse exits 0. The guard does NOT intercept 'git config' (extractBashTargets yields zero path targets, verified guard exit 0), so it is a self-service kill switch for bee's gate/reservation enforcement on Codex, reachable by the untrusted party with no privilege escalation. FIX: fail CLOSED for PreToolUse only — thread event into commandFor(script,target,event) in hooks/catalog.mjs:80 and emit for the write-guard entry: r=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$r" ] && [ -f "$r/hooks/bee-write-guard.mjs" ] || { echo 'bee write guard: cannot resolve repo root — refusing write' >&2; exit 2; }. Advisory events (SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse/SubagentStop/PreCompact/Stop) keep exit 0 per R4. Also amend spec R2/B6 (docs/specs/hook-runtime.md:111): a deny-capable checkpoint fails CLOSED when its transport cannot start — 'unknown' is not 'safe' for a deny hook. Regenerating .codex/hooks.json after the renderer fix will re-invalidate trusted_hash (Gate-4 re-trust). New fix cell required before merge.

title: Nested git root -> MODULE_NOT_FOUND -> write guard silently OFF (fail-open proves 'a git root exists', not 'bee hooks live there')
detail: CORROBORATED by two independent reviewers (security P2 + code-quality P2-1) -> promoted to P1. The transport bails only when $r is EMPTY. If the session cwd is inside a DIFFERENT git root (nested clone, vendored repo, submodule, a .spikes/ scratch repo), git rev-parse succeeds, $r is non-empty, the visible fail-open arm is SKIPPED, and 'exec node $r/hooks/bee-write-guard.mjs' dies MODULE_NOT_FOUND exit 1. Codex treats exit 1 as a non-blocking error -> write proceeds -> guard silently off. This is the ORIGINAL incident's failure mode verbatim, one layer up, and the route harness cannot see it because buildRouteFixture always copies hooks/*.mjs into the fixture root. SAME FIX as the fail-open P1: replace [ -n $r ] with [ -n $r ] && [ -f $r/hooks/${script} ] in repoCommand (hooks/catalog.mjs:72-78); for the write guard that path denies (exit 2), for advisory hooks it prints the pinned diagnostic and exits 0 (visible). Add a 5th route arm: git-init fixture with NO hooks/ dir. Consider also [ -f $r/.bee/onboarding.json ] as a repo-identity check. Fold into the same fix cell as the fail-open P1.

title: Route harness never evaluates the PreToolUse matcher — matcher 'Edit|Write|..|Grep' does NOT match Codex's apply_patch (pre-existing, not a regression)
detail: The new harness flattens hooks[].command and runs each via bash -lc, capturing group.matcher but NEVER asserting it. The configured PreToolUse matcher is Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash|Read|Glob|Grep (verified identical across pre-fix ref, plugin projection, and codex projection — so NOT introduced by this diff), while the payload sent, the adapter parse, and the tool Codex actually emits is apply_patch. new RegExp('Edit|Write|..|Grep').test('apply_patch') === false (verified). If Codex applies matchers to tool names the way Claude does, the Codex write guard is never invoked for apply_patch and the 895-line harness still prints ALL PASS — same shape as the original bug one layer up. UNPROVEN whether Codex matcher semantics actually exclude it; needs a live probe. FIX (test): add a route row asserting new RegExp(cmd.matcher).test(toolNameFor(cmd.event)) — goes RED today, converting a silent assumption into a decidable finding. Separately investigate whether the codex matcher must include apply_patch.

title: route-live-state-untouched reads LIVE .bee/state.json, so the session running the chain can trip its own suite

Fix direction: the suite should assert against a snapshot it copies first, or fixture its own state root, the way every other state suite already does.

title: Budget arithmetic should be an asserted invariant, not prose a human redoes each time
detail: The status budget is now derived by a stated rule: round the measured warm p95 up to the next 5ms multiple, add one more 5ms step, and set CI perf smoke to three times the dev number (D5's runner-variance ratio). rust-port-24 applied it correctly by hand (24.467ms -> 30ms dev, 90ms CI), but the rule lives in cell prose and a report. Fix candidate: a test in queen-bench asserting STATUS_BUDGET_MS == ceil(measured_p95/5)*5 + 5 for the recorded measurement, and that the CI figure is exactly 3x the dev budget — two one-line invariants that make every future re-measurement self-checking instead of relying on the next author redoing the arithmetic.

title: Case-fold detection degrades on filesystems that report a zero device or inode
detail: packages/bee/lib/path-identity.mjs keys its case-fold cache by device number. On a volume reporting device 0 — the no-file-index family (FAT/exFAT, many SMB/UNC shares) this module already distrusts for inode identity — every such volume shares one cache slot, so a case-insensitive share probed first hands a spurious insensitive answer to a case-sensitive one, and on exactly those volumes the identity fast path is also unusable, leaving the poisoned fold to decide. Second, same family: readOnlyCaseProbe returns dev===dev && ino===ino, which on a zero-identity volume evaluates 0===0 twice and reports case-insensitive whenever a case-flipped sibling merely exists. Both found by the wpi-1 round-2 judge, both narrow (unreproducible on this machine, needing a real zero-identity mount), both recorded as advisory rather than blocking. Fix candidate: treat a zero device the same way the module already treats a zero inode — as unusable — falling back to the path-string key and refusing the read-only probe's verdict.

title: test_cells.mjs Windows exclusion: independent permission-model cause (not path identity), euid check never fires on win32

title: canonicalPathsEqual cannot fold short-name aliasing when the path does not exist yet
detail: Windows run 30226423174 (head d41dfd40): test_herding_cli fails with 'expected marker C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...\bee-herding.enable, got C:\Users\runneradmin\...\bee-herding.enable'. Both spellings name the same file. canonicalPathsEqual resolves 8.3 aliasing through filesystem identity, but only when BOTH paths exist; here the marker is deliberately absent (that is the case under test), so it falls back to string equality, which cannot fold RUNNER~1 into runneradmin. Fix direction: canonicalize the nearest EXISTING ancestor and rejoin the non-existent remainder — the module already computes a nearest-existing-ancestor for its case probe, but the comparison does not use it. This is the first Windows evidence the local proofs could not produce, and it invalidates nothing about the fix that landed; it names the case that fix does not reach.

detail: Mirror artifact for splr-1 (commit e787819a), mandated by rust-port D1 (mjs feature-freeze mirror requirement). No Rust CLI 'state' group exists yet (crates/queen-bee/src/groups.rs only registers intent and capture; bee-parity's KNOWN_GROUPS in crates/bee-parity/src/cmdcheck.rs does not include 'state'), so the second, workflow:<id>-routed writer has no Rust twin to fix right now. title: SECURITY: write-guard containment is bypassed by the ~/ and $HOME/ spellings of an out-of-worktree path
detail: Reproduced against the live vendored hook (.bee/bin/hooks/bee-write-guard.mjs) from the repo root: 'echo hi > /home/<user>/.claude/lesson.md' is denied exit 2 with the containment message, but 'echo hi > ~/.claude/lesson.md' and 'echo hi > $HOME/.claude/lesson.md' both exit 0 — the same destination file. Cause: extractBashTargets yields the token verbatim; a leading ~/ or $HOME/ is neither absolute nor contains '..', so canonicalRelPath (bee-write-guard.mjs:65-114) resolves it against cwd as a literal directory named '~' or '$HOME' and produces an in-repo relative path, which then passes containment and flows into checkWrite. BROAD_TARGETS catches a bare '~' only (guards.mjs:1533), not '~/x'. The shell expands it and writes anywhere under $HOME at any phase. Found by the fable advisor consult during guard-memory-roots (GH #71) planning and verified independently by the orchestrator. FIX-FIRST: this must close before or with GH #71's extra-root allowlist — that feature paves exactly this path, since memory paths are conventionally written '~/.claude/...'. Fix shape: expand or deny a leading ~/ or $HOME/ (and ${HOME}/) in extracted Bash targets before containment, in BOTH runtimes, with a differential fixture.

title: test_reservation_race is flaky under full-verify concurrency

Re-run standalone 3/3 green, and the very next full run was green with 0 failures. So the loser of a reservation race can transiently report ok:false with an EMPTY conflicts array under load - either a real narrow race in the conflict-reporting path, or a fragile assertion that assumes the conflict list is populated before the loser returns. A race suite that goes red under concurrency and green alone is the kind of flake that trains people to re-run instead of read, so it should be diagnosed rather than retried.

detail: Reproduced live: feature with a capped behavior cell and NO test cell -> 'state set --feature beta --owner swarming --waive-scribing-debt' EXIT 0; the same state refuses via state set --phase scribing and via start-feature. Structural cause: each door assembles its own list of debt questions. Fix shape specified in cell p3-1 (open): one shared entry point answering 'does this feature owe anything?', every door calling exactly it, tests derived from the debt set.

title: Boundary verify picks suites by judgment; CI found a prose regression it missed
detail: test_bundle_mode.mjs pins bee-scribing routing prose and was never in MAIN's hand-picked boundary set, so a thin-body migration regression reached CI. Candidate fix: derive the boundary set from the feature's changed paths via the impact registry plus every prose-pinning suite when skills/** or AGENTS.md changed, rather than orchestrator judgment.

title: Windows CI red: test_herding 0/10 — every herdr child SPINS instead of exiting (SIGTERM watchdog)
detail: Windows workflow run 30355076562, job portable-suites(20). packages/bee/tests/test_herding.mjs: 0 passed, 10 failed, every failure 'process did not exit on its own — killed by the SIGTERM watchdog, i.e. it SPUN (the pre-fix defect). status=null' at assertNotSpun (test_herding.mjs:74). detail: All three workflows (ci.yml, windows.yml, canary.yml) are schedule + workflow_dispatch only; ci.yml:4-7 is a nightly cron that files an issue on failure and never blocks a commit. commands.test is --impacted-from-git, blind to suites outside the changed closure. detail: scripts/impact-registry.json already maps lib/state.mjs to test_misc.mjs as a direct edge and run_verify.mjs:813-909 implements --impacted-from-git against it, but planning-reference.md:162 forbids it from a per-cell verify and main-verifies retired the wave-close impacted run. vd-1 and vd-2 edited the same file and made opposite guesses. Fix: cap door runs queryRegistry(registry, cell.files, {level:1}) and requires every returned suite in cell.verify; next CLAIM (not the eventual close) runs impact_registry --check, knowledge index --check and release_manifest --check for wave-barrier debt.

title: One phase membership hand-copied six times with no parity test
detail: ['idle','compounding-complete'] is written by hand in guards.mjs:151, compaction.mjs:81, scratch.mjs:62, inject.mjs:235, intent.mjs:49, recovery.mjs:40 under three names, none importing KNOWN_PHASES, none cross-checked. guards.mjs:1294 governs write-denial. title: test_portable_paths.mjs builds its scan set from the git index with no existence filter
detail: scripts/tests/test_portable_paths.mjs:23-34 uses git ls-files -z without the existence filter vd-13 added to test_doctrine_parity.mjs:136. It does not crash (string analysis only) so it manifests as a silent coverage hole: a staged-but-unindexed file with an illegal Windows character passes green. Fix: add the filter, union with git status --porcelain, and add scripts/tests/test_scan_set_hygiene.mjs flagging any suite that reads a git ls-files list without an intervening existsSync.

title: cells cap reads top-level behavior_change but authors set trace.behavior_change
detail: vd-9, vd-10 and vd-11 all capped with trace.behavior_change false despite change_class behavior. cells.mjs:1830-1835 reads cell.behavior_change; those cells carried it only nested under trace, set at authoring time. Scribing-debt detection and the semantic goal-check judge both key off trace.behavior_change === true, so all three silently miss those obligations, and post-cap correction is refused by the tooling. Surfaced only because this was the first feature with three behavior-class cells back to back.

title: D11's completeness criterion was a manual sweep, never a standing test
detail: skills/bee-xia/references/research-brief-template.md:54 still routes proof obligations to the deleted bee-validating skill, and packages/bee/hooks/test_write_guard.mjs:664 still hand-builds the retired phase value (green only because the read path coerces it). title: A new check must be run against the diff that introduces it, before anything else
detail: dch-1 added the cap-door warning for 'your verify does not cover the suites your files touch' and shipped with a verify that did not cover the suite its own file touched: a static out-of-tree import into a file that gets vendored alone broke test_write_guard.mjs's bare fixture, fail-open swallowed it, and six assertions silently stopped running. Took dch-8 to fix. Cheapest mechanical guard: refuse a static top-level import of a path outside packages/bee from any lib file that appears in a vendoring copyLib list.

title: A suite that copies live config must derive every asserted value from that copy
detail: test_model_guard.mjs copied the real .bee/config.json into its fixtures then hardcoded 'sonnet' at eight-plus sites meaning 'a configured model'. An owner config edit turned the suite red with a message describing neither the code nor the config. Fixed in dch-9 by resolving names through the same resolvers the guard uses. The tell: the suite went red with no code change to its subject. Worth a standing check - flag a literal model/tier name in any test file that also copies the real config.

title: As a doctrine author, I want the pointer checks to read a citation naming more than one heading, so its target file and every heading it names are verified instead of the citation being skipped.
cos: The advisory file-and-heading check recognises a citation whose parenthetical carries two or more quoted headings (or a trailing non-heading item) and checks the target's existence plus every heading named, rather than matching nothing and skipping the citation entirely; the blocking pointer gate binds every heading a citation names, not only the first; negative controls prove each failure mode is detected on every run; verified by execution against fixtures, not by reading the pattern.

title: skill_lint is advisory-only, so a wrong finding survives indefinitely
detail: The pointer matcher falsely reported a reachable pointer as missing for as long as that line carried two headings. Two workers in one session read it, recorded it as 'pre-existing advisory, unrelated', and moved on - correctly, since the lint always exits 0. A false positive in a blocking check self-corrects the day it lands; in an advisory check it is stable and trains readers to skip the output. Raising skill_lint to blocking was deferred because it still carries other unresolved findings - flipping it red before those are cleared is a louder way of teaching people to ignore it. Fix those first, then flip.

title: A number recorded in a cell is a measurement with a timestamp, not a fact
detail: Planning locked a block size of 12692 bytes from an extraction-tier gather; the real size was 13396. CONTEXT.md carried the stale number into a locked decision's rationale. The executing worker re-measured before trimming and recomputed the target - had it trusted the cell it would have paid 550 bytes against a 704-byte deficit and shipped a warn-line breach. Any cell whose action depends on a threshold should re-measure at execution time; the cost is one command.

title: verify-cache-inputs.json can carry an orphan declaration that matches no suite
detail: A key in scripts/verify-cache-inputs.json whose path is not in run_verify.mjs's SUITES is inert and silently stale. Found during budget-fence-removal: deleting scripts/skill_budget_fence.mjs would have left its declaration behind with nothing detecting it. A guard asserting every declaration key resolves to a suite would close the hole. Deliberately NOT built inside budget-fence-removal - no locked decision there authorized new standing coverage (review finding A7).

title: Slice-tail test-cell guard blocks entering swarming, deadlocking the phase it protects
detail: state set refuses to LEAVE any phase while a change_class:test cell is open, including exploring->swarming and planning->swarming. But an open test cell is the correct state at that moment: planning creates the slice's trailing test cell, and cells only execute in swarming. So the guard makes the transition into swarming impossible whenever planning did what the slice-tail rule tells it to do. Hit in budget-fence-removal 2026-07-29 with bfr-3; worked around by dropping the test cell, entering swarming, and re-adding it after the implementation cells cap. The guard's intent is to block LEAVING swarming with untested behavior - it should be scoped to that exit, not to every phase exit. Error text also claims no waiver exists at any bypass level, so there is no legitimate escape.

title: Nine stale numbered-rule pointers remain outside budget-fence-removal's scope
detail: Found by bfr-6's fresh discovery sweep on 2026-07-29 (which found 18 defects where the inventory listed 13). All verified, none fixed. CONFIRMED: (1) scripts/run_verify.mjs two sites citing 'critical rule 5' for the BEE_AGENT_NAME prefix - should be rule 4; match by text, line numbers shifted after the fence comment block was removed. (2) skills/bee-hive/references/provenance.md:33 'hive law 10' for 'The agent runs the machinery' - should be hive law 9; the parenthesised critical-rule 9 there is correct. (3) packages/bee/lib/command-registry.mjs:955 "rule 12's forbidden escape hatch" for the state hand-edit ban - should be hive law 11, same defect already fixed at packages/bee/bee.mjs:4563. (4) docs/knowledge/areas/doctrine-layer/router-triage-and-the-agents-md-duplication-boundary.md:118 'rules 2-4 and 13' - should be 12. (5) same file :138 'unnumbered line under rule 14' - it sits between critical rules 16 and 17, so under rule 16. (6,7,8) packages/bee/tests/test_scratch.mjs:15, test_bundle_mode.mjs:28, test_knowledge.mjs:9 all cite 'critical rule 2' for a write-the-test-before-implementation convention; rule 2 is now feature-boundary capping and the red-first convention is rule 16 - these three may predate the byte-budget renumbering entirely and are the reason this was scoped out. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: skills/bee-hive/CREATION-LOG.md:12 - a historical creation log, frozen-log principle. Full rosters and method: docs/history/budget-fence-removal/reports/stale-rule-pointers.md. Any cell doing this owes the regen chain (touches packages/bee/ and skills/).

title: Extend the size-law regression suite to cover docs/knowledge/, where the same stale law survived three fix passes
detail: scripts/tests/test_instruction_size_law.mjs greps scripts/ for the SHAPE of a reintroduced size law, not for deleted filenames, and its negative controls prove it fires. It was never pointed at docs/knowledge/. That gap let the abolished pay-by-removal law survive in docs/knowledge/areas/doctrine-layer/placement-and-anchoring.md through THREE passes: bfr-7 fixed the Pointers bullet its cell action cited, the scribing sync fixed Business Rule R5, and only a compounding analyst found the third statement in Edge Cases Settled. A fourth lived in router-triage-and-the-agents-md-duplication-boundary.md. docs/knowledge/ is what bee knowledge context feeds to future planning sessions, so a false concept there is read as ground truth. SHAPE OF THE FIX: extend the existing suite with a sibling assertion over docs/knowledge/**/*.md BODIES for /size fence|byte budget|pay-by-remov|paid for by removing|HARD_FAIL_BYTES|WARN_BYTES/i, excluding frontmatter decisions: arrays, which legitimately name retired decisions in provenance citations. Needs a negative control like the existing ones.

title: A cell that adds or removes an auto-discovered suite owes the impact-registry regen, and nothing enforces it
detail: REGEN_GUARDS (packages/bee/lib/cells.mjs:239-258) ties a regen obligation to a cell whose files touch manifest- or ledger-covered roots. Nothing ties 'this cell adds a file under a run_verify.mjs DISCOVERY_ROOT' to 'this cell also owes scripts/impact_registry.mjs'. scripts/impact-registry.json is derived from run_verify.mjs's live SUITES (scripts/impact_registry.mjs:418) and scripts/tests/test_impact_registry.mjs:174 asserts byte-identity with a fresh build, so adding a suite reds the chain one cell later. Hit in budget-fence-removal: bfr-1 regenerated the registry, then bfr-3 added scripts/tests/test_instruction_size_law.mjs, and the slice feature-verify came back 116/117 with that single failure. Cost a whole fix-first cell (bfr-4, commit 417d0f11). SHAPE OF THE FIX: a third REGEN_GUARDS entry keyed on a cell's files touching any DISCOVERY_ROOTS path with a test_*.mjs name, requiring 'impact_registry.mjs --check' in that cell's verify. Requiring --check rather than --write is the cheaper and sufficient form: it is exactly what caught this at feature-verify time.

title: User-facing output still leaks bee jargon (cell/slice/lane, cell ids) and progress ticks get skipped — AGENTS.md rules 10+17 are stated but nothing enforces them
A locked decision that describes a code matrix must quote the function and its line range
detail: worker-conformance CONTEXT D2 restated the proof-tier matrix from memory ('lane high-risk, all classes'); the tier function leaves two classes at suite-green before the lane is consulted. The wrong phrase propagated into plan.md and into a worker's dispatch verbatim, and was caught by a worker rather than any reviewer. Planning should diff prose that describes a matrix against the function it describes.

title: Dispatch briefs are hand-composed from three sources with no consistency check
detail: In worker-conformance the plan's slice queue and the cell records disagreed on which cell owned the loosening (plan frozen, still wrong); one cell told a worker main owns the verify while the lane doctrine told it to run tests red itself; one advisor brief named a model without its tier and was refused by the model guard. Generate the brief from the cell record as the single source, and name an advisor's tier rather than its model.

title: A NEEDS_REVISION verdict reopens the cell, so a dependent repair cell can never become ready
detail: The orchestrator answered a NEEDS_REVISION by spawning a repair cell that depended on the reopened one; claim refuses on uncapped deps, so a full worker dispatch produced zero code. Either the verdict should be absorbed by the reopened cell by contract, or cells add should refuse a dep on a cell carrying an open revision verdict.

title: model-guard repairs generation-tier Agent dispatches to bee-gather, a read-only agent
detail: A dispatch carrying a leading bee-tier generation marker with subagent_type general-purpose was auto-repaired to subagent_type bee-gather. bee-gather is the read-only I/O gather agent (Read/Grep/Glob only), so an execution worker dispatch silently loses its Write/Edit/Bash capability and can only return BLOCKED. Repro: counter-teeth wave 1, four dispatches all rerouted and all four workers were unable to edit or run tests. Either the guard needs an execution-tier target agent to repair toward, or a generation-marker dispatch with a writing agent type should pass through with the model field repaired instead of the agent type. Workaround used: model param spelling without the marker.

title: close declines with the misleading unsupported-shape refusal when targeting a lane feature
detail: bee close --feature counter-teeth (a lane record, session bound to the lane, cells all capped) declines as unsupported_argument_shape on the installed 2.1.7 binary - same decline-fossil class as the route granted-arm fixed in ct-1. Reproduce and port the lane arm, or make the refusal name the real precondition.

Scope the stale-citation sweep to live documents, not closed-feature history

Exempt closed-feature CONTEXT.md, plan.md and reports/; keep the sweep on skills, docs/knowledge, AGENTS.md and docs/handbook. Decision 253fc505.

title: The verify-pipeline knowledge area still describes the deleted Node verify runner
detail: All five concepts under docs/knowledge/areas/verify-pipeline/ document scripts/run_verify.mjs, scripts/impact-registry.json and scripts/tests/*.mjs - none of which exist since the R6 Node cutover; scripts/ now holds only install.sh and install.ps1. suite-result-cache.md describes a cache whose store (.bee/logs/verify-cache.json) survives as residue while its logic is gone, and suite-topology-and-discovery.md cites a windows.yml job-level timeout-minutes of 30 that now reads 40. The area reads as active ground truth to bee knowledge context, so every planning session that touches testing is fed retired machinery. Either re-scribe the area against commands.test plus ci.yml, or mark its lifecycle retired.

title: Verify-cache literal-input finding is orphaned: its machinery was deleted with the Node runner
detail: Recorded rule from budget-fence-removal bfr-1: closureShaFor() returned null - uncacheable, no cache entry written - when ANY declared literal input was missing on disk, so the failure surfaced as an undefined cache key rather than a missing-file error; a glob input with zero matches did not have this effect, only literals did. The fixture rule was: seed EVERY declared literal input, not just one. scripts/run_verify.mjs and scripts/verify-cache-inputs.json no longer exist, so the rule has no live subject and is filed here rather than written into a spec as current behaviour. Keep it if the content-hash cache is ever rebuilt on the Rust runner: a hash helper that returns null on a missing input reports as a cache miss, never as the missing file it actually hit.

title: Review preflight lost its verification-evidence check in the Rust port
detail: reviews create no longer refuses a scope containing capped behavior_change cells with null verification_evidence; rg verification_evidence over packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/reviews.rs returns nothing. Session unreviewed-batch-20260805-a is the evidence: preflight returned cells_checked [] passed true over a scope holding 15 such cells. The old JS check was unsatisfiable (its remedy threw on an already-capped cell) so deleting it was defensible; shipping no replacement was not. Finding p2-review-preflight-lost-its-evidence-check.

title: docs/04-skills-spec.md still states the abolished 200-line skill body budget
detail: Line 14 reads 'Budgets: SKILL.md < 200 lines' and line 3 says each entry defines a body budget; budget-fence-removal (decision 8f63adb4) holds no size ceiling on instruction text is ever a standing law here. The instruction-size-law guard scanned scripts/ only, so this prose sits outside its reach. Latent - no skill violates it today. Finding p3-skills-spec-still-states-the-deleted-size-law.

title: Ten review findings landed on JavaScript the R6 port deleted
detail: Session unreviewed-batch-20260805-a finding p3-historical-findings-against-deleted-javascript records them so nothing evaporates. One deserves re-checking against the Rust runner if the suite-result cache or an --only style selector is ever rebuilt: a partially-matching selector reported green because the refusal fired only when ALL tokens matched nothing - the range's own critical pattern 20260729-a-selector-that-matches-nothing-reports-green, captured but never fixed in the runner it was mined from.

title: High-risk Gate 2 is unreachable: set_gate refuses every high-risk execution approval with a bare Ex
detail: set_gate.rs:494-500 returns Err(Err2::Ex) for any execution-component approval on a mode=high-risk record, without consulting advisor_ref; the requireFreshAdvisorForHighRisk port is unfinished R6 debt and state advisor-ref record/show are both unbuilt, so nothing can satisfy it. The bare Ex renders as 'unsupported argument shape', misdirecting the caller to their flags. Every hard-gate flag routes to high-risk, so the most dangerous class of work cannot pass its own gate. Blocks feature guard-parser-depth (the P1 write-guard parser fix). Finding p1-high-risk-gate-2-is-unreachable.

title: route --set cannot attach a route record to a lane-scoped feature
detail: With a feature started via state start-feature --as-lane, bee route --set refuses with 'no active feature to attach a route to', naming the DEFAULT pipeline's phase and feature instead of the selected lane. state set takes --lane; route --set has no equivalent selector (its --lane is the lane VALUE tiny/small/standard). So a lane-scoped feature cannot record its triage, and the claim door's no-route refusal (D4) fires on it later. Workaround used on guard-parser-depth: the lane record's own mode carries the lane.

title: bee worktree new leaves .bee/bin without the binary
detail: A worktree bootstrapped by bee worktree new has .bee/bin containing only prompts/, so .bee/bin/bee does not exist there and every bee command run from the worktree fails with 'No such file or directory'. The same command also reports 'skills: NOT synced (already present in worktree)'. Workaround: invoke the main checkout's binary with the worktree as cwd.

title: The deepened parser reads a wrapper example quoted in prose as a real target
detail: tokenize_deep unwraps a shell-wrapper payload anywhere in the command string, including inside a heredoc body. A commit message or doc that QUOTES a wrapper invocation writing to a CLI-owned path is therefore denied as if it were performing that write. Hit while committing the 2.1.10 release, whose message described the bypass it fixes; reworded to avoid the literal rather than worked around. Consider scoping the unwrap to the executable region of the command, or exempting heredoc bodies. Discovered by guard-parser-depth, the feature that introduced the unwrap.

title: Sync the gate and advisor-protocol specs to the ported precondition
detail: docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/gates.md and docs/knowledge/areas/advisor-protocol/ describe requireFreshAdvisorForHighRisk as unported and the high-risk execution gate as unconditionally refusing. As of 2.1.11 both are wrong: the precondition is live, advisor-ref record/show dispatch, and the AO13 four-anchor no-TTL rule is enforced in Rust. Also update docs/handbook/register.md's declared-but-not-built table, which now reads 21 and should read 19.

title: onboard apply resolves its template source from the binary real path
detail: Engine::locate() (packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/onboard/source.rs) walks exe-dir-first from current_exe() after symlink resolution. A feature worktree's .bee/bin/bee is a symlink into the main checkout, so an apply run from a worktree always splices the MAIN checkout's AGENTS.block.md, silently overwriting the worktree's own edited AGENTS.md and reporting neither changes_needed nor blocked_*. Uncommitted work is destroyed with no signal. Fix: prefer the explicit repo-root over the exe directory when resolving skills.source_root, and refuse rather than splice when the two disagree. Found executing cell dvl-2, 2026-08-05; see decision e3d69142.

title: bee state set --feature <other> refuses every live-feature swap: it delegates to the deleted Node runtime instead of asking the debt questions
detail: set_gate.rs:284-303 and :347-356 detect 'current feature is truthy and differs from --feature' and return Err(Err2::Ex) to hand the swap to packages/bee/bee.mjs. That tree is gone, so main.rs turns the None into emit_unsupported_shape and a non-zero exit — every real swap now refuses, debt or no debt. The native swap-debt door (open/claimed cells, active reservations, live workflows) was never ported; state start-feature has its own complete door (policy.rs:415-517) but is a different command. No test drives run_set end-to-end over a live-feature swap. Found while sweeping the stale review-p1-fixes cell p3-1, whose JS-era statement of the same door ('two of three debt questions') is now moot.

title: No verb-level test drives the workflow lifecycle: run_start_feature, run_workflows_list and run_workflows_close have zero test call sites
detail: The seams under them are unit-tested (ensure_workflow_record_for_feature idempotence, close_workflows_for_feature keep-only-named, seed_legacy_workflows gating, create_workflow refusals), but no test drives bee state start-feature / workflows list / workflows close themselves, and no integration test under crates/bee/tests touches workflow records. OpenCode binary resolution is POSIX-shaped, so the registry gate cannot run on Windows
detail: resolve_opencode_binary asks a POSIX shell and canonicalizes the answer, which follows npm's symlink to the real executable on unix. On Windows the answer is a POSIX-styled path to a .cmd shim: it does not canonicalize, and a batch script carries none of the bundled payload the derivation greps. The gate now degrades to a named skip on Windows only. Fix: resolve natively (PATH + PATHEXT) and, when the hit is a shim, follow it to the platform executable under the package root.

detail: Rust test crates carry CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR from compile time. Test binaries compiled while a session worked inside a feature worktree keep pointing at that directory; once bee worktree merge removes the tree, 14 tests fail with 'no such file or directory' on a path that no longer exists — nothing to do with the change under test. It also produced one earlier mystery red at cap time that a rerun cleared, hiding the cause. Remedy candidates: have cells finish / worktree merge touch the tests directory (or clear the test binaries) after a worktree teardown, or make the merge verify run in a clean target so the red is impossible rather than confusing.

title: One cell's work spans two directories: the control plane refuses from the worktree, the write guard refuses from main
detail: Cell, route and session-bind commands refuse inside a granted worktree (the shared control plane lives in main), while the worktree-first write guard refuses source edits from main once the feature holds a grant. A single cell therefore needs the session to move between the two directories, and dispatching a worker does not help because a worker inherits the orchestrator's working directory. Both lane-guard-deadlock cells ran inline for this reason, recorded as a named deviation. Remedy candidates: let the control-plane verbs run from a granted worktree by resolving the main store themselves (they already know where it is), or give the dispatch path a working-directory parameter.

title: Worker stalls reading a large file when the cell names a line range instead of the hits

Its last action was preparing to read verbs/cells/tests.rs (5516 lines) at the range 2045-2549 that the cell text named. The re-dispatch handed it the 11 exact rg hits instead of a range, plus an instruction to read bounded windows, and noted that all 11 already discard the return value so most may need no edit at all. title: Mark-race test is timing-scheduled and can pass vacuously
detail: verbs/status_full/tests.rs:1546-1578 (mark_pass_does_not_mark_a_session_whose_heartbeat_lands_before_the_lock) sleeps 60ms before landing the heartbeat on a spawned thread. If the thread is delayed past that point the pre-check sees a fresh record and the test passes without ever exercising the under-lock re-judgement it exists to pin. The re-judgement is independently provable at recovery_verb.rs:160-170, so the behavior is covered; the test just cannot distinguish the two mechanisms. Same family as pattern 20260812 (a guard and its tests are one model). Fix direction: drive the interleaving deterministically rather than by sleep. title: A handler declining a registry-valid shape is reported as a bad-argument error
detail: router.rs:441-452 emits 'unsupported argument shape ... what it refused is an optional flag, a flag value, or a target that does not exist' whenever the dispatcher gets None back and the registry finds nothing wrong with the argv. Since the Node fallback was deleted, every dead delegate exit in a ported handler surfaces that way, blaming the user's argv for an unported code path. Known family: decisions bda043af (state route --set), 0248c1fd (bee close for lane repos), 20969403 (set_gate, fixed by making the refusal state itself). retire-collation-guard D3 leaves this open by the user's scope choice. Fix direction: when classify() finds the argv valid, say the verb has an unported path and name the verb, rather than describing the argv.

title: Declared suite failed once under bee close and passed on five other runs, unidentified
detail: During bee close for race-test-asserts-its-premise the declared suite exited non-zero after 0.05s with 'error: test failed, to rerun pass --bin bee'. The excerpt bee close surfaced was truncated to 'me("standard"), "shaping", &[]));' — a routing/shaping fixture, not the status_full test changed in that feature. Three direct full-suite runs and a second bee close immediately afterwards all passed 1657 tests. Not reproduced, not identified, and recorded rather than dismissed: an unreproduced red is still a red that happened, and the excerpt is the only evidence of it. Fix direction: capture the full failure output at close time rather than a truncated excerpt, so the next occurrence names its test. Observed 2026-08-14.

title: Stale worker records block git add long after their dispatches finished
detail: The concurrent-worker git guard refused git add naming '2 workers are live in this checkout' when every dispatched worker of the session had already returned and capped. bee state worker prune did not clear them — it removes transient files under .bee/workers/ by filename suffix (workers.rs:248-271, 333) and never touches state.workers[]. Only bee state worker clear emptied the list. So a worker record outlives its worker and then gates a real git operation. Fix direction: either have cells finish remove the worker's own entry, or have the guard derive liveness from session heartbeats the way the active-workers view already does (state start-feature's derived check), rather than from a hand-maintained array. Observed 2026-08-14 while committing full-failure-evidence's plan.

title: Cross-worktree hold mirrors outlive the reservations they mirror
detail: dispatch prepare --claim run from main mirrors each reserved path into the cross-worktree hold ledger. When the worker caps from the granted worktree, cells finish releases the worktree-side reservations correctly — bee reservations list shows reservations: [] — but every mirror stays with released_at: null until its 3600s TTL expires. Consequence observed on full-failure-evidence: every edit ffe-2 made fired an advisory cross-worktree hold naming cells ffe-1 and ffe-2, both already capped, and the worker recorded it as a deviation for the orchestrator to reconcile. bee reservations sweep releases 0 (not expired) and bee reservations release --agent <a> --cell <c> releases 0 (the mirror is not keyed the way the release path expects). Fix direction: have the release that runs at cap clear the cell's mirrors too, or key the mirror so reservations release can reach it. Observed 2026-08-14.

title: sweep_summary_sets_agree_with_the_decision_rows_it_writes is flaky under full-suite load
detail: verbs/cells/tests.rs:2156, added by srd-1 (sweep-recovery-door). Fails under the full 16-suite parallel run and passes in isolation, reproduced twice on 2026-08-14. It uses its own tempdir (cn_root) so it is not a shared-path collision; the suspect is its exact-count assertion at :2200, lines.len() == parked.len() + unreachable.len(), which breaks if the run logs any decision row the test does not anticipate, or if a bounded lock acquisition inside the sweep times out under load and skips a claim, changing the three sets. This is very likely the same flake filed earlier the same day as unidentified — that filing had only a truncated 500-char excerpt reading 'me("standard"), "shaping", &[]));', which is tail-of-output noise rather than the failing test's name, and is exactly the blindness full-failure-evidence fixes. Fix direction: assert the rows the sweep is responsible for by content rather than by total count, and re-check the lock budget under parallel load. Owner note: this is the orchestrator's own test from two features back.

title: Write-guard Bash refusals name a shell token instead of a path when the target cannot be resolved

The guard fails closed, which is correct, but the message names a non-path so an operator cannot tell a genuine gate refusal from a target-resolution miss. Fix: when the Bash target resolver cannot map a token to a repo-relative path, say so explicitly instead of substituting the token into the gate-refusal sentence. title: worktree merge deadlocks: it demands a clean main, but the worktree-first guard refuses the commit that would clean it
cos: Observed 2026-08-14 landing traceable-runs slice 1. bee worktree merge refused with WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY because main held .bee/ bookkeeping written by the orchestrator's own state calls (cell traces, decisions, backlog). Committing that bookkeeping in main is then refused by the worktree-first guard, which classifies the bare git command as 'a feature source write in the MAIN checkout' while the active feature holds a granted worktree. Neither door can be satisfied without disabling the other, so a green slice cannot land. Note bee close already solves this exact case: after a green close it auto-commits dirty .bee/ bookkeeping path-scoped to .bee. Fix: give worktree merge the same path-scoped .bee/ auto-commit, or make the worktree-first guard exempt a commit whose staged paths are all under .bee/. Regression test: a worktree merge with only .bee/ dirt in main succeeds without any config override.

title: Three copies of scribing_debt exist; only one was reconciled with the deferred queue
cos: trun-9 reconciled drivers/close.rs::scribing_debt and status_full::unapplied_promote_proposals against the new deferred-queue records, but hooks/session_preamble/store.rs and hooks/chain_nudge.rs each keep their own pre-existing copy of the scribing-debt scan, left unreconciled and out of that cell's scope. So a debt already queued and completed can still be reported as outstanding by the preamble or the nudge. Fix: collapse the copies onto the one shared rule (deferred_debt_cleared in state_group/ledger.rs). Verify: complete a scribe queue record, then confirm neither the session preamble nor the chain nudge still reports that debt.

RESOLVED by trun-9's second and third rework rounds (trace .bee/cells/trun-9.json, commit c3312545): all SIX scribing-debt scan copies (drivers/close.rs; hooks/session_preamble/store.rs x2; hooks/chain_nudge.rs; verbs/status_full/cells.rs x2) -- not the three this item's own count claimed -- now read the shared fold state_group::ledger::scribe_queue_cells and decide via deferred_debt_cleared. Completing a scribe queue record now clears the debt on bee close's door, the session preamble, the chain nudge, bee status --json, and bee orient. Verified: hooks/session_preamble/tests.rs completing_a_scribe_queue_record_clears_the_preamble_debt_lines, chain_nudge.rs scribing_debt_clears_per_cell_once_the_queue_record_completes, status_full/tests.rs a_completed_scribe_queue_record_clears_the_status_and_orient_debt_line -- all green. title: Bash write-guard extractor treats every non-flag token after cp/mv as a write target, so a READ operand can trigger a refusal
cos: Observed live 2026-08-16: 'cargo build ... && cp packages/bee-rs/target/release/bee .bee/bin/bee' was refused naming the cp SOURCE operand (target/release/bee) as a feature source write, though the actual write target (.bee/bin/bee) is exempt. extract_bash_targets (guards.rs:607-732) collects all non-flag tokens after rm|mv|cp|mkdir|touch|tee; for cp/mv only the LAST operand (or operands after -t) is a write target. Fix: teach the extractor operand roles for cp/mv; regression: the command above passes with only .bee/bin/bee checked. Related: guard-refusal-wording grw-1 fixed the unexpanded-$ class; this is the remaining mis-extraction class (P3 in its judge record).
